title: -Ycheck reports a constructor pattern matched against List[T]() as erroneous: the typer rewrites the scrutinee to Nil and re-typing then finds :: incompatible with Nil.type
generator: wave4/harness/programs/Gen.scala, round 2 (pattern-matching family) list patterns on a generated List[Int]() literal
signature: ycheck|log|Caught java.lang.AssertionError: assertion failed: Tree has erroneous type: (head: Int, next: List[Int]): scala.collection.immutable.::[Int](...)
seed: 4000050 (programs2 round 4); first seen at 710070 in a smoke run
detail: List[Int]() match { case a :: tl => 5L; case x => x.length.toLong } compiles and prints 0, but -Ycheck:all reports 'Tree has erroneous type' for the :: pattern at every phase from typer to patmat. The typer replaces an empty List.apply() by Nil (canTranslateEmptyListToNil in Typers), keeping the expected List[Int] as the tree's type; the checker re-types the Ident Nil as Nil.type, against which a :: constructor pattern is incompatible. On the base and 2.13.18 the checker also throws a NullPointerException and no class file is written. Ordinary code rarely matches on an empty list literal; generated or macro-expanded code may.
fix_sketch: Have the rewrite produce a typed tree that keeps the widened type when re-typed (for example Typed(Ident(Nil), TypeTree(List[T]))), or have the checker accept a scrutinee whose re-typed type is narrower. No compatibility cost.
